default-governance.name: Governance
default-governance.prompt:
{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

## Governance

Verify that the implementation meets the user-defined Goal, fits the system architecture, and serves the project's purpose.

### Outcome

A clear assessment of whether the implementation satisfies all three. Begin with the verdict, then briefly explain how the work meets the Goal, fits the architecture, and supports the project's purpose, using concrete evidence from the implementation and Quality results. For each gap, describe what falls short, why it matters, and the recommended correction. Separate necessary corrections from optional improvements.

### Guardrails

- Read the context that helps explain the user's Goal, the system architecture, and the project's purpose.
- Compare the implementation with the user's desired outcome as well as the plan. Completing the plan and passing tests alone do not establish that the Goal is met.
- Look for clear responsibilities, shared behavior implemented in one place, and interfaces that remain easy to use and maintain.
- Judge design choices by how they serve the project. Allow sound approaches that differ from personal preference.
- Group related issues by their underlying cause so the next step can address them together.

default-implement.name: Implement
default-implement.prompt:
{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

## Implement

Implement the plan.

### Outcome

The plan is implemented in a way that aligns with the project's purpose and architecture. Provide a brief summary organized by plan task: what changed, any important departures from the plan and why, and any unfinished work.

### Guardrails

- Follow established code patterns and put shared behavior in one place. Fix the underlying cause rather than each symptom separately.
- Keep code focused on one responsibility and preserve stable interfaces where possible. Split mixed responsibilities into separate files. Keep files relatively small, under roughly 1,000 lines where possible.
- Prefer clear, straightforward code and abstractions that make the behavior easier to understand and maintain.

default-plan.name: Plan
default-plan.prompt:
{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

## Plan

Develop a plan to achieve the Goal's desired outcome. If the goal outcome is underspecified or is missing details add only just enough detail so that AI agents do not thrash or become confused.

### Outcome

A clear implementation plan that explains the approach and breaks the work into ordered tasks. Begin with a short description of the desired behavior and proposed solution. Use a numbered checklist, such as `Task #1 - What changes and why`. Include dependencies and important design decisions where they help implementation.

### Guardrails

- Read the context that helps explain the Goal and how the existing system works.
- Look for the underlying cause. Consider whether a missing or misused concept explains the problem, and improve that concept rather than adding fixes for individual symptoms.
- Give each task enough detail to guide implementation while leaving room for reasonable implementation choices.
- Keep the plan focused on the desired outcome. Prefer straightforward changes that fit the existing architecture.

default-quality.name: Quality
default-quality.prompt:
{{templates.purpose}}

{{templates.architecture}}

## Quality

Test the implementation. Create and groom tests to cover the behavior described in the plan.

### Outcome

Meaningful tests cover the changed behavior and pass. Provide a brief report of the behavior tested, tests added or updated, commands run and their results, and any remaining failures or gaps. Include runtime or browser test results where useful. These results support Governance's verification of the work.

### Guardrails

- Test observable behavior, including relevant failure cases and effects on existing functionality. Tests should catch defects rather than mirror the implementation.
- Keep useful tests, update tests for changed behavior, and remove obsolete or meaningless tests.
- Investigate failures, correct problems in the implementation or tests, and rerun affected tests.
- Choose tests suited to the change. Expand coverage when failures or affected behavior call for it.

fetch-goals-from-email.name: Fetch Goals from Email
fetch-goals-from-email.prompt: Fetch new email requests into the selected project's Backlog. This Skill authorizes creation of ordinary Goals from the configured mailbox. Use system.refine_executable to run `system fetch-email-goals --runtime-root <system.runtime_root> --target-root <system.project_root>`, passing each value as a separate, safely quoted argument. This one-shot capability owns secret access, the target-bound sender allowlist, MIME extraction, remote acknowledgement, deterministic Goal IDs, and durable retry records. Do not read or print the mail token, author duplicate Goals yourself, rewrite email source, or modify the request ledger. Inspect the JSON result and report the imported or recovered Goal IDs and any errors. A batch is limited to 25 remote messages; if fetched_count equals batch_limit, fetch another batch, up to ten batches per invocation, then report whether more mail may remain. Stop on a failed command and report the retained retry evidence. Fetching does not approve Goals, change Review decisions, or send email replies. Follow docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md for connection errors.

fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.name: Fetch Goals from Email on startup
fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.prompt: Queue the Custom Skill `fetch-goals-from-email` once for this startup occurrence. Run system.refine_executable with arguments `skills trigger fetch-goals-from-email --request-id startup-email-<invocation_id>`, copying invocation_id exactly from the Skill execution context supplied by Refine. Set REFINE_DAEMON_PORT to the daemon_port parameter for that command. Use safely quoted arguments. Report the queued invocation ID, then complete this startup Skill immediately. Do not wait for the child Skill: releasing this agent slot lets it run even when concurrency is limited to one. Reuse the same request ID if the command needs a retry; do not create a polling loop or fetch email directly. If the target Skill is missing or disabled, report that error without changing its configuration.

release.name: Release
release.prompt: Carry out the release request in the request parameter for the selected project. Use system.project_root as the release repository, system.runtime_root for durable operation state, and system.refine_executable for Refine commands. Read docs/runbooks/semantic-release.md in the project before acting. Use the existing system release-plan, release-prepare, and release-publish capabilities; do not reimplement version selection, candidate integration, tagging, or publication. Always pass the explicit --repo-root and --runtime-root values. Preview the requested semantic increment and report the proposed version and relevant changes. Preparation creates a normal reviewable Goal; retain its operation ID and inspect real Goal and operation evidence. Use the daemon API for asynchronous preparation when useful. Publishing requires the user's explicit publication authorization and an approved preparation; pass --confirm only when that authorization is present. Preserve review and exact-candidate checks. Reuse existing operation IDs for retries and report actual remote tag, release URL, and deployment evidence. Never infer publication success merely from a successful command or local tag.

update-metrics-hub.name: Update Metrics Hub
update-metrics-hub.prompt:
# Update Metrics Hub

You are running a Skill in Refine, alongside Goals and agents that may be working in parallel. The Refine CLI is at {{refine_executable}}; use --help to discover commands.

Keep Metrics Hub accurate and useful for understanding the target app's use of Refine.

## Outcome

Run `{{refine_executable}} hub refresh-metrics` to calculate and save the latest statistics. Read the result and open Metrics Hub to check its charts, time horizons, freshness, and data coverage. Report significant changes or missing evidence in plain language.

## Guardrails

- Use Refine's refresh command for the numbers. Do not invent completion dates, costs, or productivity claims, or change Goals to improve the statistics.
- The views cover the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, and 365 days. Rounds per Goal use Goals created in that window. Delivery uses Done Goals with a recorded final-Round integration date.
- The saved aggregate belongs to the target app's refine-state. It includes synced nodes; its freshness depends on state synchronization. It contains no Goal prompts, reports, or source code.
- If refresh fails, retain the previous snapshot and explain the problem. Keep the business interpretation distinct from the measured data.

update-refine-hub.name: Update Refine Hub
update-refine-hub.prompt:
# Update Refine Hub

You are running a Skill in Refine, which coordinates agents and Goals that may be working in parallel. The Refine CLI is at {{refine_executable}}; use --help to discover commands.

Build and maintain Refine Hub's product documentation and release notes using the requested change in Parameters.

## Outcome

Readers understand the current product and what changed. Write in plain language with only enough detail to help them use Refine. For releases, group major changes under “What you need to know” and include screenshots where they clarify the shipped interface.

## Guardrails

- Refine Hub ships from src/surfaces/refine-hub in the Refine source checkout ({{refine_checkout}}). Update those source files; the built-in Hub API is read-only. Do not put product documentation in the target application's user Hub storage.
- Check the current implementation and interface. Cover the requested release period, describe final behavior, and leave out superseded designs.
- Preserve the Hub’s visual language: clear type hierarchy, generous spacing, restrained color, and useful cards for entry points. Keep long documents readable, and check mobile, light, and dark views.
- Keep navigation and links consistent. Check changed pages, links, and screenshots in the Hub and website surfaces.
- Explain that source changes reach users when they update Refine. Follow the user's request for committing, publishing, and rebuilding.
